title: Chapter 5 Drill: Labor, Delivery, and Intrapartum Care

items.stem: A 22-year-old nulliparous woman with an epidural has been fully dilated for 3 hours and has pushed for 2 hours with reassuring fetal status and descent still occurring slowly. What is the best management?
options: Continue pushing with fetal surveillance
Proceed directly to cesarean for arrest of descent now
Stop pushing and begin a mandatory two hour rest
Place a Foley catheter within the cervix for ripening
items.explanation: Second-stage arrest in a nullipara with neuraxial analgesia is not diagnosed until at least 4 hours of pushing, or 3 hours without analgesia, and may be extended further when progress continues and the fetal heart rate is reassuring. Cesarean is premature here. Cervical ripening is irrelevant at full dilation, and a prolonged rest is not required.

items.stem: A 25-year-old woman in labor has recurrent late decelerations after most contractions, with moderate variability, while receiving oxytocin. Which initial interventions are most appropriate?
options: Proceed to immediate cesarean without other measures
Increase oxytocin to hasten delivery
Reposition laterally, give a fluid bolus, and stop oxytocin
Perform amnioinfusion
items.explanation: Recurrent late decelerations reflect uteroplacental insufficiency, and first steps are intrauterine resuscitation: lateral positioning to relieve vena cava compression, an intravenous fluid bolus, and discontinuing oxytocin to reduce contraction frequency. Immediate cesarean is reserved for failure to improve despite these measures and ongoing monitoring. More oxytocin worsens hypoxia. Amnioinfusion treats variable decelerations from cord compression, not late decelerations.

items.stem: A 35-year-old nulliparous woman has uncomplicated pregnancy with a singleton cephalic fetus and no medical problems. At 39 weeks she asks about elective induction of labor. Which counseling is best supported by randomized evidence?
options: Induction at 39 weeks doubles the cesarean rate
Induction at 39 weeks may lower cesarean rates
Induction before 41 weeks is never an acceptable plan
Elective induction raises neonatal intensive care admissions
items.explanation: In low-risk nulliparous women, induction at 39 weeks compared with expectant management showed a lower cesarean rate and fewer hypertensive disorders without worse perinatal outcomes. Induction at 39 weeks is a reasonable option after shared decision making. Claims of doubled cesarean rates or more neonatal intensive care use are not supported by the trial data, and a flat ban before 41 weeks is not guideline based.

items.stem: A 26-year-old G1P0 is receiving oxytocin for induction of labor and contractions are 2 per 10 minutes. Her cervix has changed minimally in 2 hours. What is the appropriate adjustment?
options: Increase oxytocin by small increments every 15 to 40 minutes
Double the oxytocin rate every minute
Stop oxytocin and rest for 12 hours
Switch to a bolus of methylergonovine
items.explanation: Oxytocin regimens use low-dose or high-dose protocols, starting at 1 to 2 milliunits per minute and increasing by 1 to 6 milliunits every 15 to 40 minutes until adequate contractions occur, balancing against tachysystole. Rapid doubling risks hyperstimulation. A long rest is unnecessary, and methylergonovine would cause sustained contraction and hypertension. Contraction frequency and fetal status guide each titration step.

items.stem: A 29-year-old G2P1 at 39 weeks is found to have a frank breech presentation. Which finding is a recognized criterion for planned vaginal breech delivery?
options: An estimated fetal weight above 4,500 g
An experienced provider and a flexed fetal head
A hyperextended fetal head on ultrasound
A footling presentation with a prior cesarean
items.explanation: Planned vaginal breech birth is reasonable when an experienced provider is present, institutional protocols exist, the head is flexed, the fetus is of average size, and a pelvis is adequate. Hyperextended head (stargazing), macrosomia, and footling presentation are generally contraindications because of cord prolapse and head entrapment risks. Women should be counseled about greater perinatal risk.

items.stem: A 30-year-old woman with HIV has been taking antiretroviral therapy throughout pregnancy, with a viral load below 50 copies per mL at 36 weeks. She asks about her route of delivery. What should she be told?
options: Cesarean is required for every woman with HIV
Intravenous zidovudine is required for every woman
Breastfeeding is encouraged to boost immunity
Cesarean for HIV alone offers no added benefit
items.explanation: With sustained viral suppression, the transmission risk is under 1 percent, and cesarean confers no additional benefit, so mode of delivery follows obstetric indications. Intravenous zidovudine is not needed when the viral load is 50 copies per mL or lower near delivery. Replacement feeding is advised in settings with safe alternatives, though shared decision making now applies.

items.stem: A 28-year-old G2P1 at 38 weeks is living with HIV. Her most recent viral load, drawn at 36 weeks on antiretroviral therapy, was 4,500 copies per mL. What is the recommended delivery plan?
options: Vaginal delivery with no changes in antiretroviral therapy
Induction at 41 weeks with oral therapy only
Cesarean at 38 weeks with intravenous zidovudine
Vaginal delivery with an internal scalp electrode
items.explanation: With a viral load above 1,000 copies per mL near delivery, scheduled cesarean at 38 weeks before labor or rupture lowers perinatal transmission, together with intravenous zidovudine starting 3 hours before surgery. Vaginal delivery is reasonable only at or below 1,000 copies. Internal fetal monitoring and prolonged membrane rupture raise transmission risk and are avoided.

items.stem: A 22-year-old woman at 30 weeks and 4 days is admitted with preterm contractions. Which acceleration criterion is used to call a tracing reactive at this gestational age?
options: At least 10 beats above baseline lasting at least 10 seconds
At least 15 beats above baseline lasting at least 15 seconds
At least 20 beats above baseline lasting 20 seconds
At least 5 beats above baseline lasting 5 seconds
items.explanation: Before 32 weeks, an acceleration is defined as a rise of at least 10 beats per minute above baseline lasting at least 10 seconds, because the autonomic nervous system is still maturing. From 32 weeks onward, the criterion is 15 beats for 15 seconds. The larger and smaller thresholds in the other options are not used in standard interpretation.

items.stem: A 22-year-old woman at 37 weeks has a generalized tonic-clonic seizure at home and arrives postictal. Blood pressure is 168/108 mm Hg and she is breathing spontaneously. After securing the airway, which drug should be given first to prevent another seizure?
options: Phenytoin intravenously
Diazepam intravenously
Levetiracetam by mouth
Magnesium sulfate, 4 to 6 g loading dose
items.explanation: Eclampsia is treated with magnesium sulfate, a 4 to 6 g intravenous loading dose followed by maintenance infusion, because it prevents recurrent seizures better than phenytoin or benzodiazepines. Diazepam is a rescue drug when magnesium fails and risks respiratory depression. Phenytoin was inferior in trials. Oral levetiracetam is unsuitable for a postictal patient and is not standard therapy for eclampsia.

items.stem: A 27-year-old G3P2 at 38 weeks has spontaneous rupture of membranes. A loop of pulsating cord is palpable in the vagina, and the fetal heart rate shows prolonged bradycardia. Cervix is 4 cm. What is the best management?
options: Replace the cord into the uterus and observe
Administer oxytocin to speed dilation
Elevate the presenting part and prepare for cesarean
Place a scalp electrode and wait for descent
items.explanation: Cord prolapse is an obstetric emergency, and the presenting part is elevated by a gloved hand, or the bladder is filled, while the patient assumes knee-chest or steep Trendelenburg position, and cesarean is done immediately unless delivery is imminent. Replacing the cord is ineffective, oxytocin increases compression, and waiting delays rescue. Tocolysis may help temporize while the operating room is readied.

items.stem: After delivery of the infant, a multiparous patient has a steady trickle of blood, and the placenta has not yet separated. The provider wants to hasten the third stage safely. Which intervention is the cornerstone of active management?
options: Strong fundal pressure applied before separation
Oxytocin with controlled cord traction
Manual removal started at once in every case
Routine intravenous methylergonovine as first agent
items.explanation: Active management of the third stage lowers postpartum hemorrhage and consists of a uterotonic (oxytocin first line), controlled cord traction with countertraction on the uterus, and uterine massage afterward. Fundal pressure risks inversion, routine immediate manual removal adds risk, and methylergonovine is reserved for atony that persists after oxytocin, being contraindicated in hypertension. Delayed separation beyond 30 minutes prompts evaluation for retained placenta.

items.stem: A 29-year-old G2P1 at 39 weeks and 3 days, otherwise uncomplicated, asks about stripping the membranes at her office visit. Which statement is accurate?
options: Sweeping is contraindicated in every patient who is not in labor
Sweeping reliably reduces maternal infection and bleeding
Sweeping lowers the risk of neonatal group B streptococcus disease
Sweeping raises the chance of labor within 48 hours
items.explanation: Digital separation of the membranes from the lower uterine segment releases local prostaglandins and increases the likelihood of spontaneous labor, so it is an acceptable option at term, though discomfort and spotting are common. It is not harmful in routine care, does not reduce infection risk, and has no effect on group B streptococcus disease. Sweeping is avoided with placenta previa or when membranes are ruptured.

items.stem: A 24-year-old woman at 28 weeks has asymptomatic group B streptococcus bacteriuria on a urine culture. Which management is correct?
options: Treat only if she develops fever in labor
Treat the infection now and give intrapartum prophylaxis later
Perform a rectovaginal culture at 36 weeks to decide on prophylaxis
Give prophylaxis only if she delivers before 37 weeks
items.explanation: Group B streptococcus found in urine at any colony count during pregnancy indicates heavy colonization and should be treated at diagnosis, and she also receives intrapartum prophylaxis, with no need for a rectovaginal culture at 36 weeks. Waiting for fever or preterm delivery is not part of the recommended approach. Because the bacteriuria itself signals heavy colonization, the later screening culture is skipped.

items.stem: A newborn is delivered by cesarean for a Category III tracing. Umbilical artery blood gas shows pH 7.05, pCO2 85 mmHg, and base excess of minus 4 mmol/L. How is this best classified?
options: Pure metabolic acidemia from anaerobic metabolism and lactate
Mixed acidemia with a base deficit above 12
Respiratory acidemia, with high carbon dioxide and modest base deficit
Normal arterial gas for an infant delivered after labor
items.explanation: A low pH with high pCO2 and a base deficit that is not markedly elevated points to respiratory acidemia, typically from transient cord compression, and carries a more benign prognosis than metabolic acidemia. Metabolic acidemia has a base deficit of 12 mmol/L or more, which is not present here. The pH of 7.05 is clearly abnormal, since normal umbilical artery pH is about 7.20 or higher.

items.stem: A 24-year-old woman in the third trimester has her first genital herpes outbreak at 35 weeks, diagnosed by PCR. Which statement about management is correct?
options: Treat with antiviral therapy, then continue suppression
Treat with antiviral therapy and stop after one week
Defer all therapy until labor begins
Plan cesarean at 34 weeks to avoid exposure
items.explanation: A primary infection near term carries the highest risk for neonatal herpes because maternal antibodies have not yet formed, so antiviral treatment is given for the episode and suppression continues until delivery. Cesarean is chosen if lesions or prodrome exist in labor, and stopping therapy or deferring it leaves the fetus at risk. Acyclovir is safe in pregnancy and can be given orally for the episode.

items.stem: A 29-year-old G2P1 in the second stage has a tracing showing a drop in fetal heart rate from 140 to 80 beats per minute lasting 4 minutes, then returning to baseline. How is this event defined?
options: Variable deceleration
Prolonged deceleration
Early deceleration
Late deceleration
items.explanation: A prolonged deceleration is a visually apparent decrease of at least 15 beats per minute below baseline lasting at least 2 minutes but less than 10 minutes. If it persists for 10 minutes or more, it is redefined as a baseline change. Early, late, and variable decelerations are defined by timing relative to contractions and by gradual versus abrupt onset, not by duration of this length.

items.stem: A 22-year-old G1P0 at 39 weeks has a contracted midpelvis on clinical pelvimetry, with prominent ischial spines and a narrow subpubic arch. Which pelvic type is described?
options: Gynecoid pelvis
Anthropoid pelvis
Android pelvis
Platypelloid pelvis
items.explanation: The android pelvis has a heart-shaped inlet, prominent spines, a convergent sidewall, and a narrow subpubic arch, which predisposes to arrest of descent and deep transverse arrest. A gynecoid pelvis is the classic round, favorable shape. Anthropoid pelvis has a long anteroposterior oval inlet, and platypelloid pelvis is flat with a short anteroposterior diameter. Clinical pelvimetry is imprecise, so labor progress remains the best test.

items.stem: A 32-year-old G2P1 at 38 weeks has a dichorionic twin gestation. Twin A is cephalic and twin B is cephalic, each estimated at about 2,800 g, and labor is spontaneous. What is the appropriate delivery plan?
options: Trial of vaginal delivery with readiness for cesarean
Scheduled cesarean for every twin pregnancy regardless of presentation
Cesarean only if twin B is male or the larger twin
Induction with misoprostol before 34 weeks
items.explanation: When twin A is cephalic, vaginal delivery is reasonable regardless of the presentation of twin B, provided the team can perform breech extraction or cesarean if needed. Routine cesarean for all twins is not required. Fetal sex has no bearing on mode of delivery, and induction before 34 weeks is not indicated without a maternal or fetal reason.

items.stem: A 31-year-old G3P2 at 38 weeks in the labor unit has a persistent occiput posterior fetus, severe back pain, and a slow descent in the second stage. The fetal heart rate is Category I. Which statement about this malposition is most accurate?
options: Cesarean is mandatory once the diagnosis is confirmed
Forceps are contraindicated for every posterior position
Changes in maternal position cannot influence rotation at all
Many rotate spontaneously, so continued pushing is reasonable
items.explanation: Occiput posterior is common in early labor and often rotates to anterior, particularly with adequate contractions and time. Persistent posterior position raises operative delivery risk but does not mandate cesarean. Operative vaginal delivery, including manual or instrumental rotation, is acceptable in trained hands, and hands and knees positioning may encourage rotation, though evidence for benefit is limited.

items.stem: A 33-year-old woman undergoing cesarean delivery develops sudden hypoxia, hypotension, and cardiovascular collapse right after delivery of the placenta, followed by bleeding from the incision and intravenous sites. Which diagnosis is most likely?
options: Pulmonary embolism from a deep venous thrombus
Spinal anesthesia with high block
Amniotic fluid embolism
Uterine atony without systemic effects
items.explanation: Amniotic fluid embolism produces abrupt hypoxia, cardiovascular collapse, and disseminated intravascular coagulation around delivery. It is a clinical diagnosis managed with supportive care, oxygen, vasopressors, and blood products, and rapid delivery of the fetus if undelivered. High spinal block lacks coagulopathy, atony does not cause hypoxia, and pulmonary embolism rarely brings coagulopathy. Outcomes depend on early recognition and a coordinated team response.

items.stem: A 32-year-old woman with a prior cesarean is in spontaneous labor at 39 weeks with an epidural. The team notes loss of fetal station, new sudden fetal bradycardia, and vaginal bleeding. What is the most likely diagnosis?
options: Placenta previa
Normal second stage progression
Epidural-induced maternal hypotension
Uterine rupture
items.explanation: Sudden fetal bradycardia, recession of the presenting part, bleeding, and often abdominal pain strongly suggest uterine rupture, the most feared complication of labor after cesarean, so emergency laparotomy follows. Previa presents with painless bleeding before labor. Normal progression would show descent, not loss of station, and hypotension alone would not explain bleeding or station loss.

items.stem: A 28-year-old woman at 30 weeks has cardiac arrest in the emergency department. Compressions begin and no pulse returns after 4 minutes. Which modification of resuscitation is recommended?
options: Delay compressions until the fetus is evaluated
Manual left uterine displacement, plus perimortem cesarean if needed
Place the patient in left lateral tilt on a wedge of 45 degrees
Perform compressions lower on the sternum than usual
items.explanation: Aortocaval compression in the third trimester reduces venous return, so manual left uterine displacement accompanies standard compressions at the usual hand position or slightly higher. If circulation does not return by about 4 minutes, perimortem cesarean delivery within 5 minutes is considered when the uterus reaches the umbilicus, to improve maternal resuscitation. A tilted wedge impairs compressions.

items.stem: A 25-year-old primigravida has an epidural placed at 5 cm. Four hours later her temperature is 38.2 degrees C, and there is no other source. Fetal heart rate is 165. Which statement best describes this situation?
options: Epidural fever is common, but infection must be excluded
Epidural analgesia cannot ever cause any maternal fever at all
Fever of any degree should prompt immediate cesarean
Antibiotics should be withheld until the fever persists a day
items.explanation: Neuraxial analgesia is associated with a rise in maternal temperature in a minority of nulliparous women, probably from noninfectious inflammation, but the same findings can indicate intraamniotic infection. Because fetal tachycardia and fever overlap with chorioamnionitis, evaluation and antibiotics should proceed rather than waiting. Cesarean is not indicated for fever alone. Treating with antibiotics early lowers neonatal morbidity.

items.stem: A 30-year-old multipara at 39 weeks presents in early labor. Ultrasound shows the fetal spine parallel to the cervix and the back down, with a shoulder in the pelvis. What is the appropriate delivery plan?
options: Vaginal delivery after amniotomy
Cesarean delivery for transverse lie
Oxytocin augmentation to convert the lie
Breech extraction under neuraxial analgesia
items.explanation: A persistent transverse lie in labor cannot deliver vaginally and risks cord prolapse and uterine rupture, so cesarean is performed, often with a vertical hysterotomy if the lower segment is poorly developed. Amniotomy raises prolapse risk, oxytocin may cause rupture, and breech extraction is not suitable for a singleton transverse lie at term without a skilled operator.

items.stem: A 33-year-old G2P1 at 40 weeks has a tracing showing abrupt decelerations that vary in depth and timing, each dropping at least 15 beats for 15 seconds or more, with a quick return to baseline. Which mechanism best explains these?
options: Transient umbilical cord compression
Fetal head compression during contractions
Uteroplacental insufficiency
Fetal congenital heart block
items.explanation: Variable decelerations are abrupt, with an onset to nadir under 30 seconds, and arise from cord compression that first obstructs the umbilical vein and then the artery. Early decelerations mirror contractions from head compression. Late decelerations reflect uteroplacental insufficiency and are smooth with delayed onset. Congenital heart block causes a persistent low baseline, not variable drops.

items.stem: A 27-year-old G1P0 woman at 35 weeks is in preterm labor. Her group B streptococcus status is unknown, and she has no drug allergies. Membranes are intact and she is afebrile. Which approach to group B streptococcus is correct?
options: No prophylaxis because membranes are intact
Oral amoxicillin at the start of labor
Intravenous penicillin G during labor
Wait for a rapid culture before treatment
items.explanation: Unknown group B streptococcus status with labor before 37 weeks is an indication for intrapartum prophylaxis, and intravenous penicillin G is the preferred agent. Intact membranes do not remove the indication. Oral amoxicillin does not achieve reliable levels during labor. Waiting for culture results delays protection, since delivery may occur before results return, and cultures are not required before treating.

items.stem: A 33-year-old G1P0 at 41 weeks is admitted for induction. The cervix is 1 cm dilated, 50 percent effaced, firm, and posterior, with the head at minus 2 station. What is her Bishop score?
items.explanation: The Bishop score adds points for each element: dilation of 1 to 2 cm earns 1, effacement of 40 to 50 percent earns 1, station of minus 2 earns 1, firm consistency earns 0, and a posterior position earns 0, for a total of 3. A score of 6 or lower is unfavorable and predicts the need for cervical ripening before oxytocin. Higher totals would require a softer, more anterior, more dilated cervix.

items.stem: A 31-year-old G3P2 in the second stage has a fetal heart rate tracing recorded at 70 to 80 beats per minute with spiking accelerations, and the nurse cannot see fetal movement on bedside ultrasound. Which is the most important next step?
options: Begin immediate emergency cesarean delivery under general anesthesia
Confirm the tracing is fetal, not the maternal pulse
Give oxygen and stop the epidural infusion immediately
Document a Category III tracing and wait for the next hour
items.explanation: A recorded rate of 70 to 80 with spikes during pushing may represent the maternal heart rate picked up by the external transducer. Confirming the fetal signal with a scalp electrode or ultrasound avoids mistaken intervention and also reveals a true fetal demise. Interpretation errors such as this are common in the second stage, before treating a presumed bradycardia.

items.stem: A 22-year-old G1P0 at 38 weeks has a generalized tonic-clonic seizure in labor. Blood pressure is 168/108 mmHg and urine protein is 3 plus. Which is the first-line anticonvulsant?
options: Phenytoin 1 g intravenous loading dose
Diazepam 10 mg intravenous push
Magnesium sulfate 4 to 6 g intravenously
Levetiracetam 500 mg orally
items.explanation: Magnesium sulfate is the drug of choice for treatment and prevention of eclamptic seizures, started with a 4 to 6 g load followed by 1 to 2 g per hour, and superior to phenytoin or benzodiazepines for recurrence. Blood pressure is controlled with labetalol or hydralazine. Delivery follows once the mother is stabilized. Seizure prophylaxis continues for 24 hours postpartum.

items.stem: A 27-year-old G2P1 at 39 weeks with an unfavorable cervix and no prior uterine surgery is admitted for elective induction. Which method is an appropriate mechanical option for cervical ripening?
options: Intravenous high-dose oxytocin bolus given by pump
Intramuscular carboprost injection given at once
Oral methylergonovine tablets given every 4 hours
Transcervical balloon catheter
items.explanation: A transcervical Foley or double-balloon catheter ripens the cervix by local pressure and prostaglandin release, with lower tachysystole risk than prostaglandins. Oxytocin does not ripen the cervix, being used to stimulate contractions after ripening. Carboprost and methylergonovine are postpartum hemorrhage agents, not induction agents, and methylergonovine is contraindicated in hypertension. Balloon placement is also suitable when prior cesarean scarring makes prostaglandins undesirable.

items.stem: A 33-year-old woman with a known platelet count of 62,000 per microliter due to immune thrombocytopenia requests an epidural in early labor. The count has been stable. What is the best approach?
options: Neuraxial analgesia is acceptable if the count is stable and above about 70,000
Epidural is absolutely contraindicated at any count below 150,000
Proceed with spinal analgesia without checking any laboratory
General anesthesia is required for all patients with thrombocytopenia
items.explanation: Neuraxial block is considered safe with platelet counts above roughly 70,000 per microliter when stable and without other coagulopathy, with lower counts judged individually by the anesthesiologist. Avoiding neuraxial analgesia at every count under 150,000 is unnecessarily restrictive. A count of 62,000 is borderline, so a current count, trend, and anesthesia consultation are needed. Falling counts, bleeding, or an anticoagulant would change the decision.

items.stem: A 26-year-old G1P0 at 40 weeks has a Category II tracing with minimal variability and no accelerations. Which maneuver can quickly provide reassurance about fetal acid-base status?
options: Maternal ingestion of a carbohydrate load
Pelvic examination to assess cervical dilation
Increasing the intravenous fluid rate to maximum
Fetal scalp stimulation producing an acceleration
items.explanation: A heart rate acceleration after digital scalp stimulation or vibroacoustic stimulation indicates a fetal pH above about 7.20, which allows labor to continue. A lack of response is not diagnostic of acidosis but calls for further evaluation. Dilation tells nothing about fetal acid-base status, and fluids and food do not test fetal reserve. A tracing with absent variability and no acceleration after stimulation requires further evaluation or delivery.

items.stem: A 33-year-old G1P0 at 37 weeks has a frank breech fetus confirmed by ultrasound, with normal amniotic fluid and no contraindications. She asks about external cephalic version. Which description of the procedure is correct?
options: Attempted only after the membranes have ruptured
Attempted only once active labor is established
Offered now, with tocolysis and fetal monitoring
Attempted at once in an unmonitored emergency unit
items.explanation: External cephalic version is offered at 37 weeks or later, on a labor unit with ultrasound, continuous fetal monitoring, and the ability to proceed to cesarean. Tocolysis with terbutaline improves success. Version is not attempted after rupture of membranes or in active labor, and doing so in an unmonitored emergency setting is unsafe. Contraindications include placenta previa, multiple gestation, and nonreassuring fetal status; success is moderate in nulliparas.

items.stem: A 31-year-old G3P1 at 39 weeks has had one prior cesarean, performed through a classical vertical uterine incision at 28 weeks. She asks about a trial of labor. What is the recommendation?
options: Trial of labor with oxytocin augmentation allowed
Planned repeat cesarean at 36 to 37 weeks
Trial of labor if an epidural is avoided
Induction at 41 weeks with misoprostol
items.explanation: A prior classical or T-shaped uterine incision carries a rupture risk of roughly 4 to 9 percent in labor, so trial of labor is contraindicated, and repeat cesarean is scheduled before labor begins, commonly between 36 and 37 weeks. Avoiding epidural, oxytocin, or prostaglandins does not remove the rupture risk. Delivery is performed before labor onset because contractions can precipitate rupture at the scar.

items.stem: A 29-year-old primigravida is pushing, and the clinician considers a routine episiotomy to prevent a severe laceration. Which statement best guides this decision?
options: Routine episiotomy does not protect against severe tears
Midline episiotomy reduces the risk of sphincter injury in all
Mediolateral episiotomy prevents every anal sphincter tear
Episiotomy always improves long-term pelvic floor function
items.explanation: Restrictive episiotomy use leads to less posterior perineal trauma and no excess of severe tears compared with routine use. Midline cuts actually extend more often into the sphincter. Mediolateral cuts lower extension risk but still do not eliminate injury, and long-term outcomes are not improved. Indications include a nonreassuring tracing needing rapid delivery, or shoulder dystocia in selected cases.

items.stem: A 30-year-old G2P1 in active labor has a tracing with a baseline of 150, recurrent late decelerations, but moderate variability and occasional accelerations. Which statement is most accurate?
options: Recurrent late decelerations alone prove fetal acidemia
Moderate variability is rarely found in healthy fetuses
The pattern is a Category I tracing needing no action
Moderate variability predicts absence of fetal acidemia
items.explanation: Moderate variability is the most reliable indicator that the fetal brain is adequately oxygenated and not acidemic, even when decelerations are present, though recurrent late decelerations make the tracing Category II and call for resuscitation and surveillance. Late decelerations alone do not prove acidemia. Moderate variability is normal, and Category I excludes recurrent decelerations. Management therefore combines correction of causes with continued surveillance.

items.stem: A 31-year-old G1P0 at 40 weeks has a dinoprostone vaginal insert placed for cervical ripening. After several hours, she has frequent contractions with category II tracing changes. What should be done?
options: Leave the insert and start oxytocin at once
Give a second insert for faster ripening
Remove the insert, reposition, give terbutaline
Remove it only after the cervix reaches 8 cm
items.explanation: The dinoprostone insert is removable, which is its advantage for tachysystole: taking it out stops further drug release. Supportive measures include repositioning, fluid, and oxygen, and terbutaline may be used for persistent tachysystole with abnormal tracings. Starting oxytocin or adding more prostaglandin would worsen contractions, and waiting until 8 cm risks serious fetal compromise from hyperstimulation.

items.stem: A 32-year-old G1P0 at 39 weeks needs an urgent cesarean for a Category III tracing. No neuraxial catheter is in place. Which airway risk is most important during general anesthesia in pregnancy?
options: Aspiration of gastric contents and difficult intubation
Prolonged sedation from decreased drug sensitivity
Pulmonary edema from lowered blood volume
A reduced need for preoxygenation due to higher reserve
items.explanation: Pregnancy delays gastric emptying in labor, relaxes the lower esophageal sphincter, and causes airway edema, making aspiration and failed intubation leading causes of anesthesia-related maternal death. Rapid sequence induction with preoxygenation is used. Pregnant women also desaturate quickly because functional residual capacity falls, so the claim of higher reserve is wrong. Airway management therefore requires experienced personnel and a difficult airway cart, and neuraxial techniques are preferred when time permits.

items.stem: A 26-year-old woman had a fourth-degree laceration repaired after a forceps delivery. Which postpartum plan best lowers the risk of wound complications and fecal incontinence?
options: Constipating agents for two weeks, low-fiber diet
Stool softeners, no enemas, one antibiotic dose
Daily suppositories and routine rectal thermometers
Antibiotics for 10 days plus strict bed rest
items.explanation: After sphincter repair, stool softeners prevent straining and dehiscence, and enemas or rectal instruments should be avoided. A single dose of a second-generation cephalosporin at repair reduces infection, and extended courses add little benefit. Constipating the patient promotes hard stool that strains the repair, and strict bed rest has no role. Pelvic floor follow-up is advised afterward.

items.stem: A 25-year-old primigravida has a fetal heart rate tracing with a baseline of 135, minimal variability, and recurrent late decelerations after most contractions. She is on oxytocin. Which immediate intervention is most appropriate?
options: Increase oxytocin to shorten the labor and speed the delivery
Start misoprostol to augment the contractions and hasten descent
Stop oxytocin, give oxygen and a fluid bolus, and position her in left lateral
Proceed to prophylactic amnioinfusion with nothing else
items.explanation: Recurrent late decelerations indicate uteroplacental insufficiency, and minimal variability makes this a Category II tracing that needs intrauterine resuscitation. Reduce or stop oxytocin, change position, correct hypotension, give an intravenous bolus, and consider oxygen. Increasing contractions would worsen hypoxia. Amnioinfusion treats variable decelerations from cord compression, not late decelerations, which reflect placental insufficiency. Persistent late decelerations with minimal variability would justify expedited delivery if resuscitation fails.

items.stem: A 28-year-old woman delivers a healthy infant vaginally and the placenta delivers 15 minutes later. How is the interval from delivery of the infant to delivery of the placenta classified?
options: Third stage of labor, a normal duration
Fourth stage of labor
Retained placenta, requiring manual removal
Second stage of labor, prolonged
items.explanation: The third stage runs from delivery of the infant through delivery of the placenta, normally lasting under 30 minutes, and a stage beyond 30 minutes defines retained placenta, which prompts evaluation. The second stage ends with fetal delivery, and the fourth stage is the first hour or two after placental delivery for monitoring for hemorrhage.

items.stem: A 28-year-old G3P1 at 39 weeks is receiving oxytocin for augmentation. She now has seven contractions in 10 minutes for over 30 minutes, with recurrent late decelerations. What is the first step?
options: Increase the oxytocin rate to improve her progress
Stop oxytocin and reposition her laterally
Administer methylergonovine intramuscularly now
Perform amniotomy to shorten the contractions
items.explanation: Tachysystole with an abnormal tracing is treated by reducing or stopping oxytocin, repositioning laterally, and giving a fluid bolus and oxygen if needed. A tocolytic such as terbutaline is the next step if the pattern persists. More oxytocin worsens hypoxia, and methylergonovine would cause sustained uterine tone, worsening fetal oxygen delivery. Amniotomy does not relieve tachysystole and may speed an already distressed labor.

items.stem: A 26-year-old G1P0 at 39 weeks is in labor. Her rectovaginal culture at 36 weeks grew group B streptococcus, and she has no drug allergies. Which intrapartum regimen is recommended?
options: Oral amoxicillin started once at admission to the labor unit and repeated
Gentamicin given as a single intravenous dose on admission to labor
Azithromycin given as a single oral dose when labor begins in earnest
Penicillin G 5 million units intravenously, then 2.5 million every 4 hours
items.explanation: Intravenous penicillin G is the preferred prophylaxis for colonized women in labor, with ampicillin an acceptable alternative, and it should begin at least 4 hours before delivery for best effect. Oral amoxicillin does not achieve adequate levels, and gentamicin or azithromycin alone lack reliable activity against the organism, so none of them satisfies the standard.

items.stem: A 25-year-old primigravida in labor has the head palpable abdominally at one fifth. The biparietal diameter has passed the pelvic inlet and the leading bony part is at the level of the ischial spines. Which station is this?
options: Plus 3 station
Zero station
Minus 3 station
Plus 5 station
items.explanation: Station describes the leading bony part relative to the ischial spines, in centimeters above (minus) or below (plus) the spines. Zero station means the head is engaged and at the spines. Plus 3 means crowning is near, minus 3 means the head is high, and plus 5 is at the perineum. Engagement is when the biparietal diameter has passed the inlet.

items.stem: A 28-year-old woman develops a severe positional headache 2 days after an epidural placement complicated by accidental dural puncture. The headache improves when lying flat. What is the definitive treatment if conservative measures fail?
options: Epidural blood patch
Lumbar puncture with drainage of fluid
Repeat epidural catheter with saline
High-dose oral anticoagulation
items.explanation: Postdural puncture headache arises from cerebrospinal fluid leakage and is worse upright. Initial therapy includes fluids, caffeine, and analgesics, and an epidural blood patch seals the leak, with high success. Further lumbar puncture would worsen leakage, and anticoagulation has no role and adds hematoma risk. Symptoms usually begin within 5 days; neck stiffness and tinnitus are common, and severe cases may show cranial nerve palsies.

items.stem: A 36-year-old G3P2 with two prior vaginal births and no scars is admitted for induction at 40 weeks. Her cervix is 4 cm dilated, 80 percent effaced, at 0 station. Which is the most appropriate initial management?
options: Cervical ripening with a balloon catheter first
Immediate cesarean for a favorable cervix
Vaginal misoprostol every 4 hours for a full day
Amniotomy with oxytocin as needed
items.explanation: A cervix this dilated, effaced, and low in a multiparous woman is favorable (Bishop score above 6), so ripening is unnecessary. Induction proceeds directly with oxytocin, amniotomy, or both. Amniotomy alone is often enough in multiparous women, and oxytocin is added when contractions are inadequate. A balloon or misoprostol would add risk without benefit, and cesarean is unwarranted for a favorable cervix.

items.stem: A 30-year-old woman at 36 weeks who is Rh negative and never received immune globulin arrives with decreased fetal movement. The tracing shows a smooth, regular sine-wave pattern at 3 to 5 cycles per minute for 25 minutes. What is the clinical significance?
options: A benign finding after recent maternal analgesic use at term
A normal pattern with moderate variability and reactivity
Severe fetal anemia or hypoxia, so delivery is considered
A sign of fetal sleep cycling in a healthy fetus
items.explanation: A sinusoidal pattern is a smooth, undulating wave with absent short-term variability, and is associated with severe fetal anemia from fetomaternal hemorrhage, Rh alloimmunization, or hypoxia. It is a Category III tracing when sustained for at least 20 minutes. Do not confuse it with the pseudosinusoidal pattern seen after opioid analgesia, which is brief and has a more irregular shape.

items.stem: A 26-year-old G2P1 at 37 weeks in labor reports sudden severe constant abdominal pain. The uterus is rigid and tender, with dark vaginal bleeding, and the fetal tracing shows recurrent late decelerations. Which finding would most support the likely diagnosis?
options: Retroplacental clot with a firm, tender uterus
Painless bright red bleeding with a soft uterus
Fetal heart rate stable with a normal uterine tone
Bleeding that begins after rupture with fetal bradycardia
items.explanation: Placental abruption in labor classically produces constant pain, a hypertonic tender uterus, dark bleeding, and nonreassuring tracings, with hemorrhage often concealed. Painless bright bleeding with a soft uterus suggests previa, and bleeding with sudden fetal bradycardia after membrane rupture suggests vasa previa. Normal tone and stable heart rate argue against significant abruption. Coagulation studies and cross-matched blood should be ordered early.

items.stem: A 25-year-old G1P0 at 39 weeks and in early labor has a cluster of painful vesicles on the vulva. She has had two prior outbreaks, and membranes are intact. Which delivery recommendation applies?
options: Vaginal delivery with intravenous acyclovir
Vaginal delivery after covering lesions with a dressing
Induction with oxytocin and amniotomy
Cesarean delivery, as active lesions are present
items.explanation: Active genital lesions or prodromal symptoms such as burning or tingling in labor are indications for cesarean delivery to avoid neonatal herpes, ideally before prolonged rupture, though cesarean after rupture may still help. Antiviral treatment or covering lesions does not remove the indication. Amniotomy would increase exposure and is avoided. Neonatal herpes carries high mortality and neurologic morbidity, which justifies surgical delivery.

items.stem: A 28-year-old G1P0 at 40 weeks has regular contractions. Her cervix is 5 cm dilated, 90 percent effaced, and the head is at 0 station. She received no analgesia. Four hours later the cervix is unchanged despite adequate contractions. By current criteria, which statement applies?
options: Active phase arrest is present and cesarean is indicated
Arrest cannot be diagnosed before active labor begins
A protracted active phase is present and needs observation
Second-stage labor has begun and pushing should start
items.explanation: Active labor is now defined as beginning at 6 cm, so a cervix at 5 cm is still in the latent phase, and arrest of dilation cannot be diagnosed before 6 cm. This patient is therefore in a slow latent phase, managed with observation, rest, and oxytocin if indicated, so cesarean is premature. Second stage requires full dilation.

items.stem: A 29-year-old G4P3 who uses cocaine presents at 36 weeks with sudden pain and bleeding, a firm uterus, and fibrinogen of 90 mg/dL. Which complication is she at greatest risk of developing?
options: Hyperfibrinogenemia with venous thrombosis
Isolated thrombocytosis
Disseminated intravascular coagulation
Polycythemia with hypervolemia
items.explanation: Abruption releases tissue factor from the decidua into the maternal circulation, consuming clotting factors and producing disseminated intravascular coagulation, so a low fibrinogen predicts severe hemorrhage and needs transfusion planning. Cocaine, tobacco, hypertension, trauma, and prior abruption raise the risk. Thrombocytosis and polycythemia are not expected, and fibrinogen falls rather than rises. Monitoring fibrinogen guides cryoprecipitate replacement.

items.stem: A 26-year-old G1P0 at 39 weeks has been pushing for 2 hours with a nonreassuring tracing. The vertex is occiput anterior at plus 3 station, the cervix is fully dilated, membranes are ruptured, and the bladder is empty. Which statement about vacuum delivery is correct?
options: The membranes must first be intact
The cervix may be only 8 cm dilated
The station must be above the spines
All standard prerequisites are met
items.explanation: Operative vaginal delivery requires full cervical dilation, ruptured membranes, a known fetal position, an engaged head at station plus 2 or lower, adequate maternal analgesia, an empty bladder, and no suspected fetal bone or bleeding disorder. Each requirement is present here, so the procedure may proceed. Intact membranes, partial dilation, and a high station all contraindicate the procedure and would need correction first.

items.stem: A 28-year-old G2P1 at 39 weeks with ruptured membranes and oligohydramnios has recurrent variable decelerations with each contraction. Variability is moderate. Which intervention is likely to reduce the decelerations?
options: Transcervical amnioinfusion with isotonic fluid
Intravenous terbutaline bolus every 15 minutes
Immediate maternal sedation with a benzodiazepine
Fundal pressure to speed the second stage
items.explanation: Amnioinfusion replaces missing amniotic fluid, cushioning the umbilical cord and reducing recurrent variable decelerations. Position change is tried first. Terbutaline helps tachysystole and late decelerations, not simple cord compression. Sedation has no effect on the tracing, and fundal pressure would increase cord compression and risk uterine injury. Amnioinfusion is most useful when oligohydramnios is present; repositioning and correcting tachysystole are tried first.

items.stem: A 29-year-old G2P1 at 40 weeks has a vacuum delivery. After the head delivers it retracts against the perineum, and the shoulders fail to deliver with gentle downward traction. What is the most appropriate first maneuver?
options: Fundal pressure by an assistant
McRoberts maneuver with suprapubic pressure
Pulling harder on the fetal head
Immediate symphysiotomy in the labor room
items.explanation: A retracting head, the turtle sign, signals shoulder dystocia. McRoberts positioning hyperflexes the maternal thighs, flattening the sacral promontory, and is combined with suprapubic pressure applied just above the pubic bone. Fundal pressure impacts the shoulder further, and traction on the head risks brachial plexus injury. Symphysiotomy is a last resort reserved for failed maneuvers.

items.stem: A 35-year-old G1P0 receives an epidural bolus and soon has hypotension to 80/45 mmHg with a drop in fetal heart rate. What is the best immediate treatment?
options: Supine positioning with the head of the bed lowered flat
Intravenous oxytocin bolus to restore uterine tone
Left lateral position, fluid, and phenylephrine or ephedrine
Stopping all monitoring to prevent further alarms
items.explanation: Sympathetic blockade causes vasodilation and hypotension, and aortocaval compression worsens it, so treatment is left uterine displacement, a fluid bolus, and a vasopressor, with oxygen for fetal compromise. Supine positioning aggravates compression. An oxytocin bolus can cause further hypotension, and monitoring must continue. Phenylephrine is often favored because it protects fetal acid-base status, and a fluid preload helps but cannot fully prevent hypotension.

items.stem: A 29-year-old at 38 weeks has ruptured membranes for 14 hours, a temperature of 38.5 degrees C, fundal tenderness, and a fetal baseline of 175. What is the first-line antibiotic regimen?
options: Oral azithromycin alone for seven days
Ampicillin and gentamicin intravenously
Intravenous metronidazole alone until delivery
Intravenous vancomycin alone until delivery
items.explanation: Intraamniotic infection is treated with broad-spectrum antibiotics started promptly, typically ampicillin plus gentamicin, and delivery follows by obstetric indications because infection alone does not require cesarean. An additional dose after cesarean covers anaerobes, with clindamycin or metronidazole added then. Single agents with narrow coverage are inadequate. Antibiotics continue until delivery, with one further dose after cesarean; doses after vaginal birth are not needed.

items.stem: A 30-year-old G1P0 woman is in labor. Which factor most increases her risk of an obstetric anal sphincter injury at delivery?
options: Use of warm perineal compresses
Delivery in a semirecumbent position
Forceps-assisted delivery
Prior cesarean delivery
items.explanation: Operative vaginal delivery, especially with forceps, is the strongest modifiable risk factor for obstetric anal sphincter injury, along with nulliparity, macrosomia, and midline episiotomy. Warm perineal compresses in the second stage reduce injury. A semirecumbent posture is not a major risk factor. Prior cesarean delivery involves no vaginal birth and does not raise perineal laceration risk in itself.

items.stem: A 26-year-old woman at 39 weeks has a known complete placenta previa and begins contractions. Which statement about labor induction is correct?
options: Induction with oxytocin is safe if she is closely monitored
Amniotomy may be used to hasten labor safely here
Misoprostol is the preferred agent in this setting
Induction is contraindicated, so cesarean is planned
items.explanation: A complete placenta previa covers the cervical os, so descent of the fetus would cause catastrophic hemorrhage, and vaginal delivery is contraindicated. Other absolute contraindications to labor include vasa previa, prior classical cesarean, active genital herpes, and transverse lie. Neither oxytocin, amniotomy, nor misoprostol makes labor safe when the previa persists. Cesarean is therefore scheduled at 36 to 37 weeks in stable patients.

items.stem: A 27-year-old G1P0 at 39 weeks in active labor has a tracing with absent baseline variability and recurrent late decelerations. Resuscitative measures for 30 minutes do not change the pattern. What is the best next step?
options: Expedite delivery for a Category III tracing
Continue expectant monitoring for another full hour or so
Give a higher oxytocin dose to hasten the progress
Repeat the cervical examination before any action
items.explanation: Absent variability with recurrent late decelerations is a Category III tracing, which is abnormal and predicts acidemia. Intrauterine resuscitation is attempted while preparing for delivery, and if the pattern persists, prompt delivery is required, vaginally if imminent and otherwise by cesarean. Continued observation or more oxytocin delays rescue and risks neonatal injury. Preparing the operating room should begin while resuscitation is under way.

items.stem: A 29-year-old G2P1 at 37 weeks has a history of genital herpes and is currently asymptomatic with no lesions or prodrome. Which antenatal intervention is recommended to reduce the chance of an outbreak at delivery?
options: Cesarean delivery scheduled at 39 weeks regardless
Weekly viral cultures from the cervix until delivery
No treatment since she is asymptomatic
Suppressive acyclovir or valacyclovir from 36 weeks
items.explanation: Suppressive antiviral therapy starting at 36 weeks reduces recurrences and cesarean rates in women with a history of genital herpes, and vaginal delivery is appropriate if no lesions or prodrome are present at labor. Routine cesarean for history alone is not recommended, and surveillance cultures are not useful. Treatment typically uses acyclovir or valacyclovir at standard doses, and counseling about transmission is offered.

items.stem: A 28-year-old G1P0 in labor has a fetus whose presenting part is the face, with the mentum anterior. The cervix is 7 cm and the tracing is Category I. What is the appropriate management?
options: Perform immediate cesarean delivery for face presentation
Apply vacuum extractor to the fetal face
Allow labor to continue, as vaginal delivery is possible
Convert the presentation by internal podalic version
items.explanation: A face presentation with the chin anterior can deliver vaginally because the neck flexes under the symphysis, so labor may continue with close monitoring. Chin posterior, or mentum posterior, cannot deliver vaginally unless it rotates anteriorly, and requires cesarean. The vacuum is contraindicated on the face, and internal podalic version is not used for a singleton.

items.stem: A 30-year-old multipara has an uncomplicated delivery. During excessive cord traction, a mass appears at the introitus, with shock and no heavy bleeding. The fundus cannot be palpated abdominally. What is the diagnosis?
options: Uterine inversion
Retained placenta with atony
Uterine rupture
Vaginal hematoma
items.explanation: A mass in the vagina, an absent fundus on abdominal exam, and shock out of proportion to blood loss indicate uterine inversion, often from cord traction on a fundal placenta. Management is immediate manual replacement while the uterus is relaxed, with a tocolytic or nitroglycerin if needed. Atony causes a boggy fundus, rupture presents with pain, and a hematoma lacks a missing fundus.

items.stem: A 23-year-old woman with eclampsia has a second seizure 10 minutes after the 6 g magnesium loading dose. What is the next step?
options: Switch to phenytoin and stop magnesium sulfate
Give another 2 g of magnesium sulfate intravenously
Observe, since a second seizure is expected
Proceed to cesarean without further medication
items.explanation: A recurrent seizure on magnesium is managed with another bolus of 2 g, or up to 4 g, while confirming airway, oxygenation, and the drug level. Phenytoin has inferior efficacy, and seizures should not simply be observed. Eclampsia alone does not require immediate cesarean, and delivery is planned once the mother is stable. Persistent seizures despite this regimen warrant neuroimaging.

items.stem: A 23-year-old G1P0 at 39 weeks, 6 cm dilated, has shallow, gradual decelerations that begin and end with the contractions and mirror their shape. Variability is moderate and the baseline is 130. What should be done?
options: Continue routine monitoring
Perform immediate cesarean delivery for fetal distress
Start amnioinfusion for presumed cord compression
Administer a tocolytic agent for uterine tachysystole
items.explanation: Early decelerations are symmetric, gradual, and coincide with contractions, reflecting vagal response to fetal head compression during labor. They are benign and need no intervention when variability is moderate. Cesarean and tocolytics are for abnormal patterns, and amnioinfusion is used for recurrent variable decelerations from oligohydramnios or cord compression, which this tracing does not show.

items.stem: A 34-year-old G2P1 with one prior low transverse cesarean is at 40 weeks and desires a trial of labor. Her cervix is unfavorable. Which agent should be avoided for ripening?
options: Transcervical balloon catheter
Oxytocin after ripening
Misoprostol given by the vaginal route
Amniotomy once the cervix is favorable
items.explanation: Misoprostol, and generally high-dose prostaglandin regimens, raise the risk of uterine rupture in women with a prior cesarean or other uterine scar, so it is avoided. A mechanical balloon catheter does not raise rupture risk meaningfully, and carefully titrated oxytocin is acceptable. Amniotomy is also acceptable when the cervix permits. These options keep trial of labor safe and reasonably likely to succeed.

items.stem: A 24-year-old at 38 weeks in labor has been ruptured for 20 hours. Her temperature is 38.4 degrees C, maternal heart rate is 112, and the fetal baseline is 180 beats per minute with moderate variability. What is the most likely cause of the fetal heart rate finding?
options: Fetal head compression from descent
Cord compression with a nuchal loop
Maternal opioid effect on the fetal heart
Intraamniotic infection with fetal tachycardia
items.explanation: Fetal tachycardia, defined as a baseline above 160 beats per minute for more than 10 minutes, is a classic sign of intraamniotic infection, along with maternal fever and tachycardia. Moderate variability suggests the fetus is not currently acidotic. Head compression gives early decelerations, cord compression gives variable decelerations, and opioids typically reduce variability rather than raise the baseline.

items.stem: A 24-year-old primigravida at 39 weeks is in labor. During descent the fetal head rotates so the occiput turns from a transverse position to face directly anterior beneath the pubic symphysis. Which cardinal movement does this describe?
options: Engagement with synclitism
Internal rotation
External rotation (restitution)
Extension of the head
items.explanation: Internal rotation brings the sagittal suture into the anteroposterior diameter of the pelvic outlet as the vertex reaches the level of the ischial spines. Engagement is passage of the biparietal diameter through the inlet. Extension follows, as the occiput pivots beneath the pubic arch. Restitution and external rotation occur after the head delivers, when the head realigns with the shoulders.

items.stem: A 34-year-old G3P2 at 40 weeks is undergoing a primary cesarean delivery for arrest of labor. She weighs 95 kg and has no allergies. Which antibiotic regimen is appropriate for surgical prophylaxis?
options: Cefazolin 2 g intravenously after the cord is clamped
Gentamicin 5 mg per kg given as a single dose
Cefazolin 2 g intravenously before skin incision
Ampicillin 2 g intravenously, repeated every 6 hours
items.explanation: Prophylactic cefazolin 2 g given within 60 minutes before skin incision lowers endometritis and wound infection, and is increased to 3 g for women who weigh 120 kg or more. Giving the dose after cord clamping is less effective than preincision administration. Gentamicin alone and prolonged ampicillin do not provide adequate surgical prophylaxis. Adding azithromycin is advised for laboring women or those with ruptured membranes who undergo cesarean.

items.stem: A 30-year-old woman at 38 weeks is admitted in labor. The tracing shows a baseline of 140 beats per minute, moderate variability, and accelerations. How is this tracing classified?
options: Category II
Category III
Indeterminate pending further observation
Category I
items.explanation: A Category I tracing is normal, with a baseline of 110 to 160 beats per minute, moderate variability, no late or variable decelerations, and early decelerations or accelerations that may be present. It strongly predicts normal fetal acid-base status, so routine care continues. Category II is the broad intermediate group, and Category III includes absent variability with recurrent decelerations or a sinusoidal pattern.

items.stem: A 30-year-old G1P0 at 40 weeks has a Bishop score of 4. The team chooses misoprostol 25 mcg vaginally every 4 hours. She has no prior uterine surgery. Which finding would require stopping the next dose?
options: More than five contractions per 10 minutes with decelerations
Cervical dilation progressing from 1 cm to 3 cm
Maternal temperature of 37.2 degrees C at the time
A reactive tracing with moderate variability and accelerations
items.explanation: Misoprostol is effective for ripening, but it can cause tachysystole, defined as more than five contractions per 10 minutes averaged over 30 minutes. With fetal heart rate abnormalities, further doses are withheld and intrauterine resuscitation begins. Progressive dilation is the desired effect, and a normal temperature or reassuring tracing gives no reason to stop; these findings reflect expected, safe progress during ripening.

items.stem: After McRoberts and suprapubic pressure fail to release the anterior shoulder, the clinician inserts a hand into the vagina and applies pressure on the anterior surface of the posterior shoulder to rotate it. Which maneuver is this?
options: Zavanelli maneuver
Rubin or Woods screw maneuver
Gaskin all-fours maneuver
Mauriceau Smellie Veit maneuver
items.explanation: Rotating the shoulders in a corkscrew manner, by pressure on the anterior or posterior shoulder, reduces the bisacromial diameter and is the Rubin or Woods maneuver. Zavanelli means replacing the head and proceeding to cesarean. The Gaskin position uses hands and knees, and the Mauriceau Smellie Veit maneuver delivers the aftercoming head in breech delivery.

items.stem: A 33-year-old woman undergoing a repeat cesarean delivery has hematuria in the Foley bag after a difficult dissection of adherent bladder. Which is the most likely site of injury?
options: Distal ureter
Urethra
Bladder dome
Bladder trigone
items.explanation: The bladder is the urologic organ most often injured at cesarean, usually at the dome when dissecting from scar after prior surgery, and presents with hematuria, a visible defect, or gas in the collecting bag. Repair is in two layers with catheter drainage. Ureteral injury occurs less often, usually near the uterine vessels, and urethral injury is unlikely from the abdomen.

items.stem: A 27-year-old G1P0 is scheduled for forceps-assisted delivery for maternal exhaustion. The fetal head is at plus 3 station, occiput anterior. Compared with vacuum extraction, forceps delivery is more likely to cause which outcome?
options: Maternal perineal and sphincter injury
Fetal subgaleal hemorrhage with scalp swelling
Fetal cephalohematoma from scalp traction
A higher rate of fetal retinal hemorrhage
items.explanation: Forceps delivery has a higher rate of maternal third and fourth degree lacerations and vaginal trauma than vacuum, though it succeeds more often. Vacuum delivery is associated with more neonatal scalp injuries, including cephalohematoma, subgaleal hemorrhage, and retinal hemorrhage. The choice depends on operator skill, and both are acceptable when prerequisites are met. Operator experience and fetal station often guide which instrument is chosen.

items.stem: A 25-year-old woman has an uncomplicated term vaginal delivery of a vigorous newborn. What is the recommended timing for umbilical cord clamping?
options: Clamp immediately to permit blood gas sampling in all
Clamp only after pulsations stop, always at 10 minutes
Clamp within 10 seconds to limit neonatal jaundice
Delay at least 30 to 60 seconds
items.explanation: In vigorous term and preterm infants, delaying clamping for 30 to 60 seconds improves hemoglobin and iron stores, and in preterm infants lowers intraventricular hemorrhage. The small increase in jaundice requiring phototherapy is acceptable with monitoring. Immediate clamping is reserved for neonates needing resuscitation or for maternal emergencies, and waiting ten minutes is not recommended practice.

items.stem: A 27-year-old G1P0 receives oxytocin for augmentation of labor for 14 hours and becomes confused, with a headache and a witnessed seizure. Serum sodium is 118 mEq/L. Which mechanism best explains this?
options: Oxytocin-induced magnesium toxicity from the infusion
Antidiuretic effect of oxytocin causing dilutional hyponatremia
Eclampsia from severe hypertension in labor
Amniotic fluid embolism with consumptive coagulopathy and collapse
items.explanation: Oxytocin has structural similarity to antidiuretic hormone, and prolonged high-dose infusion in a hypotonic carrier produces water retention and dilutional hyponatremia, which can cause seizures. Treatment is stopping oxytocin and giving hypertonic saline. Blood pressure here is not described as elevated, no magnesium was given, and amniotic fluid embolism presents with collapse and coagulopathy. Using an isotonic carrier and avoiding prolonged high-dose infusion prevents this problem.
